From: Maya Patel <maya@apture.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jul 2025 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Trial runway question + usage attached

Hi Rishi —

Thanks for the quick onboarding last week. We ran a heavier set of tests this week and burned through more tokens than our estimate (attached). Two asks from procurement and engineering:

1) Can Redwood give us a 3-week runway extension on the existing timeboxed trial, or
2) alternatively, can you offer a short-term credit bucket (tokens/credits) we can consume this month while procurement finalizes a PO?

Procurement is asking whether an invoice or a voucher approach is easier — they want minimal contract edits. Our engineering team would prefer the flexibility of credits so they can ramp tests without waiting.

High level numbers (attached): ~1.1M tokens last 7 days; peak concurrent requests were during model-compare runs. We expect similar burn for the next 2–3 weeks if we proceed.

We need a decision by Thursday 7/31 to avoid dropping tests. Appreciate options and any quick guidance on billing flow.

Thanks,
Maya Patel
Head of ML Platform
Apture Health

Attachment: apture_weekly_usage.csv (CSV, 98KB)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Maya Patel <maya@apture.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jul 2025 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Trial runway question + usage attached

Hi Maya —

Appreciate the data — that helps. Two pragmatic paths we can offer today so you don't have to pause:

Option A — Short committed add-on (fast path)- 30 day mini-commit: $7,500 flat (covers up to 1.5M tokens) + 10% discount on overage. Invoice now, apply to next invoice if you convert to a reserved plan. No contract amendment needed beyond an addendum.

Option B — Flexible burn-pool (engineering-first)- 1x credit voucher: equivalent of $6,000 in token credits (non-refundable, usable over 45 days). No change to trial dates; credits applied immediately to your account so your team can continue testing. Requires signoff from procurement for charge, but we can issue a purchase order invoice or a quick DocuSign amendment — your choice.

Notes:
- If procurement prefers minimal paperwork, Option A is the cleanest (we can push the invoice through and attach it to the HubSpot deal).
- If engineering needs immediate ability to spin tests up and down without changing trial gating, Option B gets you unblocked faster.
- Either option preserves the trial for evaluation metrics reports we will keep separate from production billing.

I've attached a short proposal PDF with both options and the suggested amendment language so your legal/procurement can review quickly.

If you want, I can hold a 20-minute call tomorrow AM to walk procurement through the invoice flow.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0198

Attachment: redwood_proposal_v1.pdf (PDF, 45KB)

Hi Maya / Rishi —

Quick finance/legal notes on the two options so Apture procurement knows what to expect:

Option A (30-day mini-commit / invoice)- Invoiced as a one-off professional services invoice. We can net 30 payment terms; we will not tie this to a long-term commitment unless you want to convert. If you later convert to Dedicated or Reserved we will apply a credit per the addendum.

Option B (credit voucher)- Treated as a prepayment. For accounting: we will record as deferred revenue until credits are consumed. If your accounting team needs an invoice for the voucher purchase we can issue it immediately with the voucher reference.

Other items to confirm:
- Tax jurisdiction / W-9 needed for US companies — procurement usually provides this.
- PO number: if Apture requires a PO, please share to ensure matching.
- SLA exception: extending trial window doesn't change SLAs; if you ask for elevated uptime/latency commitments during the trial add-on we'll need to surface that in an SOW.

If you share the procurement contact we can route the DocuSign or generate the invoice and cc them. Happy to keep this lightweight.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Head of Finance Ops (Contracts)
Redwood Inference

Maya —

Quick update from our side: Rishi and Kim are aligned. Given your engineering timeline we can greenlight Option B (the flexible credit voucher) to get you unblocked today. Process:

1) I can send a DocuSign amendment that records a one-time credit purchase (no change to core trial terms).
2) Once signed, we apply the voucher to your Apture account and engineering can resume runs immediately.
3) Procurement can follow up with payment via standard invoice (we'll issue an invoice referencing the voucher if you need it for PO matching).

Please confirm who in procurement should receive the DocuSign (email + PO number if available). If you prefer the invoice-first approach instead, say the word and we’ll issue one immediately for Option A.
